title: Supetar Cost Guide 2027: Prices for Stay, Food, Ferry
metaDescription: Supetar, Brač costs for 2027: ferry fares, hotels from about €60, meals at €15–35, scooters and daily budgets in euros, with tips for saving money.
content:
## How Much Does a Trip to Supetar Cost?

Supetar is the main ferry port on the north coast of the island of Brač. It is cheaper than Hvar or Bol, but not cheap in July and August. A budget traveler can manage about €70–90 a day. A couple in a mid-range apartment with restaurant dinners should plan for €150–250 a day, excluding car costs. Prices below are based on 2026 figures. Expect small increases in 2027, so treat them as a floor.

### Daily Budget by Travel Style

| Style | Per person per day | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Budget | €70–90 | Hostel bed or shared room, bakery breakfast, one casual meal, local bus |
| Mid-range | €120–180 | Apartment or 3★ hotel share, one konoba dinner, beach extras |
| Higher-end | €200+ | 4★ hotel, seafood dinners, boat or taxi transfers |

The lowest figures only work outside July and August. Accommodation is the biggest cost, and it rises sharply in peak season.

## Getting to Supetar: Ferry Prices

The Jadrolinija car ferry (line 631) runs from Split to Supetar. The crossing takes 20–50 minutes depending on the vessel, and the high-season timetable has up to 14 sailings a day, from 05:00 to 23:59.

### Jadrolinija Car Ferry Fares

Lower season runs 1 January–31 May and 1 October–31 December. High season runs 1 June–30 September.

- Adult: €4.40 (lower) / €6.50 (high)
- Child 3–12: €2.20 / €3.20
- Bicycle: €4.30 / €6.20
- Motorcycle: €9.10 / €12.90
- Car up to 5 m: €18.20 / €26.10
- Car over 5 m or over 2 m high: €32.90 / €40.30
- Camper up to 5 m: €32.90 / €42.90

The car price does not include the driver's own ticket. A driver with a car in August pays about €32.60 each way.

### Krilo Fast Catamaran

The Krilo catamaran is for foot passengers only. It costs €10 one way, with no child or senior discount, and takes about 20 minutes. Tickets are sold online or at a kiosk on Gat Sv. Petra in Split port. It is a seasonal service, so check the timetable for your dates.

### Should You Bring a Car?

Bringing a car costs about €52 return in high season, plus parking. Supetar's centre is compact and walkable. Most visitors are better off walking on and renting a scooter from about €30 a day, or a small car locally. Several rental agencies are close to the ferry dock. Take the car only if you are staying in a remote villa or travelling with a lot of luggage and children.

## Accommodation Prices in Supetar

Booking platforms show a wide range. The cheapest rooms and apartments begin around €50–60 a night. Typical hotel rates run about €60–130 for two people. In peak season, sea-view apartments and villas can pass €200.

### Apartments and Private Rooms

Apartments are the most common option in Supetar. A simple apartment costs about €50–100 a night outside peak weeks. Expect €100–200 in July and August for places near the waterfront. Many hosts require a minimum stay of 3–7 nights in summer, which reduces flexibility.

### Hotels

- Hotel Osam is a 4★ adults-only hotel in the centre with a rooftop bar. It scores about 9.2 on review platforms and starts around €120, with summer rates of €150–250.
- Aminess Vival Casa Velaris is a 3★ hotel with a pool, about 300 m from the beach. It starts around €70.
- Hotel Villa Adriatica is a 4★ hotel with a pool, from about €105.
- Waterman Beach Village and the Aminess Velaris Resort are larger resort complexes, with rates from about €80–110.

Hotel Osam is excellent, but the rooftop view is the main selling point. If you are not drinking up there, a well-reviewed apartment on the same street gives better value.

### Hostels and Budget Beds

Beds start at about €20 a night, but Supetar is pricier than Split. Anyone visiting only for the day should stay in Split and take the ferry.

## Food and Drink Costs

Supetar's waterfront restaurants charge more than the streets one or two blocks back. Prices below are per person.

- Bakery breakfast (burek or pastry plus coffee): about €4–7
- Fast food or casual meal: €10–20
- Standard konoba lunch or dinner with a drink: €20–35
- Grilled fish by weight: expect €60–90 per kilo, which makes a fish dinner for two around €70–110 with sides and wine
- Coffee: about €2–3
- Beer in a café: about €4–5

Konoba Vinotoka and Palute Restaurant are two established places in the centre. Vinotoka serves Dalmatian dishes such as grilled fish, octopus salad, gnocchi and lamb, with meals at about €20–35 including drinks. Palute falls in the €15–30 range.

Avoid ordering fish without asking the price per kilo first. The weight-based price is where most bill surprises come from.

### Groceries

Supermarkets in town are the cheapest way to cover lunch. A picnic of bread, local cheese, tomatoes and fruit costs about €6–10 per person. The market near the waterfront sells produce, olive oil and the local wine.

## Getting Around the Island

Supetar's centre is small and the main beaches, including Vlačica and Banj, are within a 5–15 minute walk. For the rest of Brač, you need transport.

- Taxi or pre-booked transfer Supetar to Bol: about €60–75 per car, about 40 minutes
- Scooter rental: from about €30 a day
- Arriva bus: buses are timed to ferry arrivals and leave from the station by the dock. A bus ticket costs a fraction of a taxi, so check fares at the station

Bol, with Zlatni Rat beach, is about 35–40 km away. A taxi to Bol for four people costs around €15–19 each, so splitting a car works well.

## Activities and Extras

The town's beaches are free. Sunbeds and umbrellas at beach bars cost about €10–20 a day for a pair, depending on the location. Water sports and boat tours cost more. Budget about €17 a day on average for activities, according to typical traveler budgets. Walking the Supetar peninsula and the Mala Banda area costs nothing. Add €1–3 for a day-trip bus ticket or parking in the town.

## Money-Saving Tips

1. Travel in May, June or late September. Ferry fares are lower until 31 May and from 1 October, and accommodation drops 30–50% against August.
2. Walk on the ferry. A car adds €18–26 each way, plus the driver's ticket.
3. Book apartments with a kitchen. Breakfast and lunch at home cut food costs by about a third.
4. Eat one street back from the waterfront. Prices are lower, and the food is often just as good.
5. Share taxis to Bol or rent a scooter for the day instead of paying for several single rides.
6. Check the tourist tax at booking. A small per-night fee per adult is usually added and it varies by season.

## Insider Notes

- The 05:00 and late-evening ferries are quieter, and car queues in July and August can run for hours. Foot passengers skip most of that.
- Tickets for the car ferry can be bought at the port. Pets in carriers travel at half the adult fare.
- Cash is rarely required, as cards are accepted in most restaurants, but small bakeries and market stalls may prefer cash.
- Weekend rates in booking systems are often lower than weekday rates, so shifting a check-in by a day can save money.

faq.question: How much does a day in Supetar cost?
faq.answer: A budget day costs about €70–90 per person. A mid-range day with a shared apartment and restaurant dinner costs about €120–180. In July and August, expect the upper end or more.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Split to Supetar?
faq.answer: An adult foot passenger pays €4.40 in the lower season and €6.50 from 1 June to 30 September. A car up to 5 m costs €18.20–26.10. The Krilo catamaran costs €10 for foot passengers.

faq.question: Is Supetar expensive compared with other Croatian islands?
faq.answer: Supetar is cheaper than Hvar and Bol, and the ferry is short and frequent. Summer apartments and waterfront restaurants are still pricey. Prices drop clearly outside July and August.

faq.question: How much does a meal cost in Supetar?
faq.answer: A casual meal costs about €10–20 per person. A konoba meal with drinks runs about €20–35. Grilled fish sold by weight raises the bill quickly.

faq.question: How much does a hotel cost in Supetar?
faq.answer: Hotels usually cost about €60–130 a night for two, with 4★ properties like Hotel Osam from about €120 and up to €250 in summer. Simple apartments begin at around €50.

faq.question: Do you need a car in Supetar?
faq.answer: No. The town is walkable and the ferry for a car costs €18.20–26.10 each way, plus the driver's ticket. A scooter from about €30 a day or a taxi covers trips to Bol.

faq.question: How much is a taxi from Supetar to Bol?
faq.answer: A taxi or pre-booked transfer costs about €60–75 per car for the 40-minute trip. Splitting it between four people makes it comparable with other transport options.

quickAnswer: Supetar costs roughly €70–90 per person per day on a budget and €150–250 on mid-range trips in summer. The Split ferry costs €4.40–6.50 on foot. Simple apartments start around €50 a night, hotels about €60–130 and up. Restaurant meals cost €15–35 per person. Scooters rent from about €30 a day.
